oneLiner: Closed at 29,187.55 Friday, down 2.5% on the day and 5.49% on the week, about 6.5% below the record close of 31,224.47 set on October 6.
intro: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,187.55 on Friday, October 16, down about 2.5% on the day and 5.49% on the week, roughly 6.5% below its October 6 record close of 31,224.47. Chip stocks fell for an eighth straight session as doubts about AI spending and debt spread, and oil prices climbed.

performance.heading: How the index has done
performance.body: The strip above tracks QQQ, the ETF that follows the Nasdaq-100, through the same week. After finishing last week just off its record, the Nasdaq-100 gave back roughly 5.5% over five sessions, with Friday among the sharpest days. The longer-period cards show how this pullback sits against the longer trend.

chart.heading: The trend against its moving averages
chart.body: The daily chart above plots QQQ against its 50- and 200-day moving averages. After this week's slide, the chart may show how far price has moved from those averages and whether the longer trend still looks intact.

levels.heading: Where the nearby levels sit
levels.body: The October 6 record close of 31,224.47 is the nearest marker above for the index, with Friday's close about 6.5% below it. This week's slide has opened a much wider gap than a week earlier, when the index finished just off its record. The Price zones and Key levels cards above show where the nearby levels sit on QQQ today.

signals.heading: Momentum in plain words
signals.body: A drop of about 5.5% in a week, led by chip stocks, may show momentum fading after the October 6 record close. The panel above shows today's RSI and MACD readings on QQQ, which can differ from the index.

change.heading: The weekly and monthly pattern
change.body: Close to close, the index fell about 5.5% this week, after finishing the prior week just off its record, and about 2.5% on Friday alone. Chip stocks fell for eight sessions in a row, their longest losing run since 2008. The tabs above show the daily, weekly and monthly changes on QQQ.

marketRead: The Nasdaq-100 ended the week at 29,187.55, down 5.49% on the week and about 6.5% below its October 6 record close of 31,224.47. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell about 3.8% on Friday, its eighth straight daily decline and longest losing run since 2008, as investors questioned whether AI revenue can cover the spending behind it. CoreWeave, an AI cloud company that reported about $51 billion of debt at the end of June, fell about 12% on Friday.

Rates and oil added pressure. September consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier, and the 10-year Treasury yield sat near 5.1% on Friday. Brent crude rose about 3.7% to near $110 a barrel. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh declined to signal the October decision, and markets increasingly expect the Fed to hold this month, with CME FedWatch putting a December rate rise at about 89%. Among chip names on Friday, Broadcom fell about 4.5% and AMD about 6%.

We could not confirm a dated figure for the share of Nasdaq-100 members above their 200-day average, so none is shown. The optimistic case is that the 10-year yield, which touched above 5.3% at points this week, has since eased, and that the pullback has so far been led by chip stocks. The cautious case is that financing worries may spread from smaller AI borrowers to larger names, while high oil and yields keep pressure on growth valuations.

The coming weeks may hinge on third-quarter earnings, with Tesla and Meta among the early reports next week, and on whether results ease the doubts about AI returns. The Fed's late-October meeting and the path of oil prices may also shape how the index moves.

points.label: Catalyst
points.text: Chip stocks fell for an eighth straight session as worries about AI spending and debt spread; CoreWeave fell about 12% on Friday.

points.label: Record
points.text: The index set a record close of 31,224.47 on October 6; Friday's close sits about 6.5% below it.

points.label: Rates
points.text: The 10-year yield was near 5.1% on Friday, and Brent crude rose to near $110 a barrel.

watchDown: Financing worries around AI infrastructure spread from smaller borrowers such as CoreWeave to larger technology names.
Chip stocks extend their eight-session slide as doubts about AI returns persist.
Oil prices and Treasury yields climb further, pressing on growth company valuations.
The pullback broadens beyond chip stocks into other large technology names.
watchUp: Chip stocks stabilise after eight straight daily declines.
Third-quarter results from large technology companies ease the questions about AI spending.
Oil prices and the 10-year yield ease from current levels.
The index recovers toward its October 6 record close of 31,224.47.
